issues.legal_issue: A reservation is not validly made unless the prescribed particulars are verified, and a finding that no reservation was made is not shown to be legally erroneous when that verification is not established.
material_facts: The landowner submitted an application in the prescribed form to the local revenue officer seeking to reserve land.
The record did not show that the local revenue officer verified the correctness of the particulars in the application.
The reviewing authority found that no reservation had been made, and that finding was challenged in a writ proceeding.
issues.conclusion: A valid reservation required verification of the application particulars; because the record did not establish that verification, the finding that no reservation had been made was not shown to contain an error of law.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 5(1) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, read with Rules 3, 5 and 6, a reservation is subject to verification of the particulars by the Patwari. In a writ challenge to the revisional order, the appellant had to establish that the order was without jurisdiction or was vitiated by an error of law apparent on the record.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_revisional_finding: A party challenged a revisional authority’s finding in a writ proceeding.
predicates.reservation_application_submitted: A landowner submitted an application seeking to reserve land.
predicates.patwari_verification_not_shown: The record did not establish that the local revenue officer verified the application particulars.
predicates.finding_of_no_valid_reservation_not_show: The finding that no valid reservation was made was not shown to be legally erroneous.

issues.definition: When a revisional finding is challenged in a writ proceeding, an application without established verification does not show that the finding of no valid reservation was legally erroneous.

issues.legal_issue: Land selected from a landowner’s permissible area under the later selection procedure is treated as area reserved under the Act and is not available for purchase by a tenant under the tenant-purchase provision.
material_facts: A tenant had occupied the land continuously for the period required to apply to purchase it.
The landowner had not previously exercised the right to reserve land under the initial procedure, but later selected the land as the landowner’s permissible area under the subsequent procedure.
The reviewing authorities held that the tenant could not purchase the selected land.
issues.conclusion: Selection under the later procedure is a form of reservation: the selected land is area reserved under the Act, so the tenant cannot purchase it under the tenant-purchase provision. The same interpretation means that the selected area falls within the area from which a tenant may be evicted under the applicable eviction provision.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(3), 2(5-A), 5(1), 5-B, 9(1)(i) and 18 of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act must be read in light of the Act’s purposes of preserving a permissible area for a landowner’s self-cultivation and conferring rights on tenants in surplus land. The selection under section 5-B gives a landowner who did not previously reserve land another opportunity to identify the permissible area; the selected land is therefore area reserved under the Act for sections 9 and 18. The Court approved Karam Singh v. Angrez Singh and Angrej Singh v. Financial Commissioner, Punjab.

predicates.tenant_purchase_claim: A tenant sought to purchase land held in the tenancy under a statutory tenant-purchase procedure.
predicates.landowner_did_not_use_initial_reservatio: The landowner had not exercised the initial procedure for reserving land.
predicates.landowner_later_selected_permissible_are: The landowner later selected the land as part of the landowner’s permissible area under a statutory selection procedure.
predicates.later_selected_area_is_treated_as_reserv: Land selected through the later procedure is treated as reserved area and cannot be purchased by the tenant.

issues.definition: When a tenant seeks to purchase land and the landowner, having not used the initial reservation procedure, later selects it as permissible area, the selected land is treated as reserved and is unavailable for purchase by the tenant.
